summary: 24600231 (32 statin-eligible low/moderate-risk adults on a TLC diet, pantethine 600 then 900 mg/day for 16 weeks) met its primary endpoint with lower LDL-C versus placebo (P=0.006 at week 16) plus lower total and non-HDL cholesterol. The larger companion trial 21925346 (n=120) agrees but is abstract-only and carries no credit. Credit is scoped to pantethine lipid outcomes, kept separate from pantothenic acid as Dr. Pham required. Fourth-ruling boundary applied: lipid outcome only; clinical-event prevention excluded.

applicability.studied_population: Adults at low to moderate cardiovascular risk with raised LDL-C following a TLC diet, taking pantethine 600-900 mg/day for 16 weeks; not pantothenic acid and not a statin substitute.

identity.chemical_form: Pantethine (Pantesin HF55, pharmaceutical grade, 300 mg per tablet); not pantothenic acid

population.description: 32 adults aged >=21 at low to moderate CVD risk with LDL-C above TLC goal (statin-eligible by ATP-III), predominantly white women, randomized after a 4-week TLC diet; 24 completed.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, triple-blinded, placebo-controlled trial with diet control (TLC diet throughout), 16 weeks.

outcomes.name: Primary: change in fasting LDL-C over 16 weeks; lower versus placebo at week 8 (P=0.020) and week 16 (P=0.006)
Total cholesterol lower at week 16 (P=0.040); non-HDL-C lower by week 16 (P=0.042); triglycerides not changed

limitations: Very small (32 randomized, 24 completers) and short; lipid surrogate only, not a cardiovascular-event trial or a substitute for statins.
Authors include employees of Daiichi Fine Chemical (Pantesin maker) and Kyowa Hakko USA; conducted by a contract research organization.
Dr. Pham's returned decision requires keeping pantethine distinct from pantothenic acid (vitamin B5); this evidence does not transfer to calcium pantothenate or pantothenic acid.
The step-up from 600 to 900 mg/day gave no measurable extra benefit at week 12 (Discussion); no dose threshold is implied.
TLC diet four week run in continued throughout; not medication substitution or CVD event trial.

Dr. Pham's fourth ruling set (2026-10-28) boundary: tight lipid claim; LDL-C change is not prevention of clinical cardiovascular events (2026 ACC/AHA advises against relying on supplements for dyslipidemia).
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Three tablets daily; weeks 1-8 two active plus one placebo tablet, weeks 9-16 three active tablets
co_therapies: Therapeutic Lifestyle Change (TLC) diet from 4-week lead-in throughout

source_provenance.location: Methods (eligibility, TLC diet, randomization, investigational product Pantesin HF55 300 mg tablets, primary end point); Results Table 1, Figure 1-2; author affiliations

normalization.basis: Assigned pantethine mass per day (300 mg tablets).

population.description: 120 North American adults at low to moderate CVD risk on a TLC diet (60 per group).

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, triple-blinded, placebo-controlled trial with 4-week TLC diet lead-in, 16 weeks.

outcomes.name: Total cholesterol and LDL-C lowered versus placebo (P<.005), sustained

limitations: Full text not open access; only the PubMed abstract was retrieved. Primary end point designation, completer numbers and effect sizes were not verifiable, so this context carries no credit.
Same research program and design as 24600231; not independent replication by a separate group.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.reported_regimen: 600 mg/day baseline to week 8, 900 mg/day weeks 9-16

freshness_search.query: pantethine[tiab] AND (cholesterol OR lipid* OR LDL OR triglyceride* OR dyslipid* OR hyperlipid*) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt] OR randomized controlled trial[pt])

supplementary_queries.query: pantethine[tiab] AND (cholesterol OR lipid* OR LDL OR triglyceride* OR dyslipid*)
supplementary_queries.note: unfiltered sensitivity check; newest 60 titles screened

freshness_search.screening_rule: Kept human placebo- or active-controlled pantethine lipid trials and syntheses newer than 24600231 (2014). The unfiltered titles were otherwise animal, mechanistic, neurodegeneration or pre-2014.

read.title: Efficacy and tolerability of coenzyme A vs pantethine for the treatment of patients with hyperlipidemia: A randomized, double-blind, multicenter study.
read.finding: 2015 double-blind RCT, 216 Chinese adults with moderate dyslipidemia: CoA 400 U/d vs pantethine 600 U/d for 8 weeks, with no placebo arm. Pantethine lowered TG 16.5% from baseline and CoA was superior for TG. LDL-C did not differ between groups. Active comparator only.

freshness_search.conclusion: confirms: no synthesis and no newer placebo-controlled pantethine trial exists after 24600231. The only newer trial is active-controlled and cannot test efficacy. Credit stays limited to LDL-C lowering in the studied population, with no clinical-event credit (fourth ruling).
